feature: The dev app says how far behind it is
summary: The dashboard and the loop now say out loud when "Photonz Dev" on your disk is older than the code, how many commits behind it is, and that a held playtest lock is the reason. Nothing releases the lock for you.
setup: The dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8791, Summary tab. Nothing to turn on. Right now the lock really is held and the app really is 12 commits behind, so the warning is live.

try.do: Open http://127.0.0.1:8791 and read the top right of the Summary hero, under the walk sweep line.
Read the amber strip under the hero: how old the build is, how many commits changed the app since, and that the lock is why.
Run queue/bin/testing.sh in a terminal. Under "holding since" it prints the same sentence.
Run queue/bin/refresh-dev-app.sh. It refuses on the lock, prints the same sentence, and leaves the app alone.
If you are done working in the app, run queue/bin/testing.sh off, then queue/bin/refresh-dev-app.sh to rebuild it now.
Reload the dashboard. With the app current, the strip and the hero line are both gone.

evaluate: Does the strip tell you what to do next without already knowing what the playtest lock is?
Is amber right for an app two days and twelve commits old, or should that be red?
Would naming the newest commit's subject ("A turning layer says where its pivot is once") help you spot that your own reported fix is missing, or is the count enough?
Did the small amber line in the hero corner catch your eye at all, or did you only see the strip?
With nothing holding the lock the page stays quiet for 30 minutes while the refresh compiles. Too long, too short?
rough: The picture is the dashboard in a browser, not the app. This task changed the dashboard and two loop scripts and touched no app code, so no scripted walk applies and none was run.
It stacks under the locked-screen strip, so on a Mac that is both locked and holding the lock you get two amber strips at once. They say different things, but it is a lot of amber.
It says how many commits are missing, never which. "12 commits behind" is honest but it cannot tell you your Save fix is one of them.
The 30 minute quiet window before an unlocked gap is called out is a guess at how long a refresh takes, not a measurement.

A commit landing in the same second the bundle was written reads as older than the build. A build takes minutes, so this cannot happen in a real refresh, but it is worth knowing the comparison is that tight.
